title: backlog.py landings counts only landings of items this clone's history holds
goal: backlog.py landings reads only the ops rows whose item has a file in this clone's git history (git log --all of kb/_self/backlog), so rows of other clones' or early synthetic runs' items are left out, and its count line says how many rows it left out

run: import re, subprocess, sys; sys.path.insert(0, '_tools'); import bl_stall; files = set(re.findall(r'kb/_self/backlog/([A-Z]{2}-[a-z0-9]{8})[.]json', subprocess.run(['git', 'log', '--all', '--name-only', '--format=', '--', 'kb/_self/backlog'], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout)); want = sum(1 for r in bl_stall.ops_rows('.') if r.get('event') == 'land.end' and r.get('item') in files and isinstance(r.get('ms'), (int, float))); r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '_tools/backlog.py', 'landings'], capture_output=True, text=True); got = [int(m) for m in re.findall(r'^land[.]end\s+n=(\d+)', r.stdout, re.M)]; sys.exit(0 if r.returncode == 0 and got == [want] else 1)

notes: Review of SP-4f4m3noq (2026-10-22): of 4867 items with a land.end row only 1263 have an item file in this clone's history; 3374 TK- and 230 ST- have none, ~4700 rows dated 2026-10-02/03; land.end n=6681 failed=2208 p95=195946 are inflated, and a row is an attempt (retries count), not a landing. bl_stall.ops_rows reads the host-wide spool and every committed sidecar.
